newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati supporters go to full trial.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati supporters go to full trial.

text.p: A Jakarta court will hear evidence next week in the trials of 64 Indonesians charged with taking part in riots this summer, after defence moves to drop the charges were rejected on Wednesday, a court official said.

Budiman (Eds: one word), clerk of the court for criminal matters at the Central Jakarta State Court, said judges in the five separate trials rejected defence arguments, known as exceptions, calling for the charges to be dropped. The defence had said there were legal flaws in the prosecution's case.
"The judges decided not to accept the exceptions and as such the court cases will now enter the evidence-taking stage and they were all adjourned until next Monday," Budiman told Reuters.

The accused are supporters of Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri. They were arrested after their occupation of Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) headquarters in Jakarta -- aimed at protesting Megawati's ouster as party leader -- ended with a police raid on July 27.
They are charged with assault and disobeying police in rioting that followed the raid. Five people were killed in the rioting, the worst in Jakarta in 20 years.
Another 60 Megawati supporters facing the same charges will return to court on Thursday when judges in another batch of five trials are expected to rule on the same motion, he said.
Lawyers have said presentation of evidence could last two months.
Political analysts have said the government sought to sideline Megawati as it feared she could cut into the ruling Golkar party's vote in the 1997 general elections.

Megawati has filed lawsuits against election officials for refusing to accept her list of candidates for next year's elections and against the mayor of East Jakarta for closing down a temporary headquarters she set up last month.
The head of her legal team, R.O. Tambunan, said he expected the first hearings in the two lawsuits to begin next week.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only political groups legally permitted to contest elections.
